description: Every lab route mapped to the finding an honest scanner should or must not produce. Positive cases pin the expected category, detector and verification level; negative cases are findings that would be false alarms. The verification bounds are part of the contract: a scanner that claims 'confirmed' for the reflection route, or 'clean' for the exposure route, fails the oracle.
notes: P5 uses prefix matching on purpose: every default lab route is served without Content-Security-Policy, so per-route instances are instances of one condition.
N4 is a catch-all: any nuclei template matching the lab other than the git-config bait is a false alarm for this profile.
Negative cases are evaluated before positive ones, and the most specific case wins, so a generic catch-all can never swallow a specific expectation.

cases.rationale: The marker is reflected verbatim into HTML, but execution context was never tested. The finding must stay info/unverified; claiming observed or confirmed here would be dishonest.
The client fully controls the Location destination, proven behaviorally by a reserved .invalid canary that is never followed.
A quote mutation yields a SQLite error signature: evidence of an injection path, not proof of exploitability, so 'inferred' and nothing stronger.

An exposed git config must be reported whether the native detector or the official nuclei template found it: the expectation is about the exposure, not the tool. When nuclei is installed both may fire, and either result satisfies the case.
Default lab routes send no Content-Security-Policy; each instance on a default route is an observed hardening gap. Hardened routes (/safe, /item, /public) must stay clean.
The lab's listening port must be observed through the production port pipeline: by nmap when it is installed, and by the native TCP connect scan when it is not.
The safe route accepts the parameter and echoes nothing; any reflection finding is a false positive.
The safe route sends a Content-Security-Policy header; flagging it would mean headers were not actually read.
The login route redirects to a fixed same-origin path and ignores the next parameter; the canary must not be reflected into Location.
The catalog route is static text with no database behind it; a quote mutation changes nothing and no error signature may appear.
With the configs exposure subset, the only template that may fire is git-config. Anything else matching the lab is a false alarm for this profile.

The native git detector must fire on exactly one thing: the served repository bait at /.git/config. A hit anywhere else (a 200 HTML catch-all, a prose page) is a false positive; the specific P4 case absorbs the real bait, so anything landing here is an over-claim.
